items.headline: MCP's 2026-07-28 spec moves the core from stateful to stateless request/response
items.source_excerpt: The 2026-07-28 MCP specification changes the core transport from stateful sessions to stateless request/response. Stateless servers can be scaled horizontally behind an ordinary load balancer, with no sticky sessions and no shared session store. The change breaks cross-version compatibility, and Roots, Sampling, Logging, and Dynamic Client Registration are deprecated with a 12-month runway.

items.headline: Kimi K3 — largest open-weight model yet (2.8T params, 1M context)
items.source_excerpt: Kimi K3 is the largest open-weight model released to date, at 2.8T parameters with a 1M-token context window. Open weights at this scale change the build-vs-buy calculation for agents, where per-call cost compounds across many calls per task. The tradeoff is raw capability against serving cost and latency.

items.headline: Paper: iStar — implicit step rewards for multi-turn agentic RL
items.source_excerpt: iStar assigns per-step implicit rewards so an agent receives credit on intermediate actions rather than only on the final outcome. It reports a +6.3% success improvement on WebShop and VisualSokoban. Results are benchmark-only, and the paper notes that step-reward design is where the difficulty concentrates.

items.headline: Terminal-Bench 2.1: GPT-5.6 Sol (89.5%) edges Opus 5 (89.1%)
items.source_excerpt: On Terminal-Bench 2.1, GPT-5.6 Sol scores 89.5% and Opus 5 scores 89.1% — a 0.4-point gap at the top of the coding-agent leaderboard. The frontier is effectively a near-tie, which reduces how much the model itself differentiates a coding agent relative to the harness and eval design around it.

items.headline: OpenAI closes record $122B round ($852B post); Anthropic at $965B
items.source_excerpt: OpenAI closed a record $122B round at an $852B post-money valuation; Anthropic is valued at $965B. Frontier-lab rounds at approximately $1T valuations set the pricing umbrella that downstream builders operate under, moving both API pricing and talent costs.

items.headline: Global VC hit record $510B in H1 2026; AI took ~80% of Q1 dollars
items.source_excerpt: Global venture funding reached a record $510B in H1 2026, with AI companies taking roughly 80% of Q1 dollars. Capital is concentrating into AI at valuations priced for perfection, leaving non-AI startups competing for the remaining ~20% of dollars.

items.headline: House advances AI OVERWATCH Act; Blackwell export ban, H200 to case-by-case
items.source_excerpt: The House advanced the AI OVERWATCH Act, which bans export of Blackwell-class chips and moves H200 exports to case-by-case licensing. Chip access becomes a policy variable rather than only a supply constraint, so vendor and region choices can shift based on where a company and its customers operate.
